title: Joint coordinate-pair mass
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. For any $x,y\in\Omega$, the joint probability mass at $(x,y)$ under the retention-and-resampling experiment is $\pi(x)$ times the conditional probability mass of obtaining $y$ from $x$ under the coordinate noise distribution.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
